name: Perceived Street Vitality in Central Tianjin: Pairwise Comparison
description:
Method replication: participants compare 30 pairs of street views from central Tianjin, each shown as four directions (front, right, back, left) in a 2 × 2 grid, and click the one with a higher level of perceived street vitality, or choose "Equal / no obvious difference"; the images are not the paper's stimuli (79 re-fetched Baidu street view locations in Heping, Hedong, Hexi, Hebei, Nankai and Hongqiao districts, 2019–2023).

Original study: Zhang, Zhong, Wu, Wang, Liu, Ji, Yu & Hou (2026), Sustainability 18(10), 5165. Baidu street views were requested in four directions at 143,956 points in central Tianjin and merged into 1024 × 768 images; 1,333 of them were each compared at least 15 times by 330 respondents who had lived, studied or worked in Tianjin (10,000 comparisons, left–right order randomised, an equal option allowed). Q-scores trained an EfficientNetV2 model, and geographically weighted machine learning related streetscape elements to the predicted vitality.

Differences from the original study: (1) newly fetched Baidu street views instead of the authors' images, which are not released, with the bottom of each view cropped to remove the camera car; (2) 30 random pairs per participant, close to the paper's average of about 30 per respondent; (3) the background questions follow the categories of the paper's Table 2, with the question wording written for this template.
author: Zhang, Zhong, Wu, Wang, Liu, Ji, Yu & Hou
